note: Generated by tools/read_planarian_scan.py from the scan's outputs, the tool's own entry list, the atlas's table and the dossier's InterPro release: do not edit. The entries the scan added are in data/proteins/planarian/interproscan_added.tsv; the table's own column is unchanged. Not plainly permissive: NCBIfam (CC BY-SA 4.0, share-alike) and CDD (no stated terms, used by the decision of 18 November 2026 that a database whose provider states no terms may be used for this scan where it is publicly available). Each entry keeps the databases that found it, so that entries found by NCBIfam alone or by CDD alone can be counted or taken out without a new scan. docs/PLANARIAN_ATLAS.md says what the scan is.

tool.name: InterProScan
tool.is: the tool that ran the databases' signatures on the proteins, not a database: it is named here and not classed as a source
tool.citation: Jones and others (2014) InterProScan 5: genome-scale protein function classification. Bioinformatics. PMID 24451626.
tool.citation_from: InterPro's page on citing it and InterProScan's own (saved as cite_interpro_citing.html and cite_interproscan_citing.html)
tool.options: the lookup service of precalculated matches switched off (-dp); InterPro entries and Gene Ontology terms added to each match (-iprlookup, -goterms); outputs tsv and json

run.days_from: the date column of the outputs' TSV lines
run.left_out: PROSITE and SMART (not free to commercial users), SUPERFAMILY (a registration with its staff), PIRSF and PIRSR (PIR asks commercial users to inform it and report yearly), MobiDB-lite (it bundles a program under an academic licence agreement), FunFam (not needed), and SignalP, TMHMM and Phobius (vendors' licences)
run.counted: a chunk counts only when both its outputs exist and its pass's log says it ended with exit 0; a match is one signature on one protein, as the tool found it, with its own cutoffs

AntiFam.release_from: no output of a counted chunk holds a match of it, so the outputs state no release

Coils.terms: The program ncoils (GNU General Public License, as the terms folder's note records): a program, not a database, with no InterPro entries; only its counts are kept

dropped_not_in_dossier_release.why: an entry the dossier's InterPro release does not hold is dropped, and counted here (the first hundred named)

table_entries_not_found.of: the table's own entries on the proteins at least one counted pass ran on, by cause: no database run on the protein has a signature in the entry (by the tool's list); one has and did not match; the entry is not in the tool's list

entries.as_pairs: each count is of pairs of a protein and an InterPro entry

could_see.universe: the InterPro entries of the type Family in the dossier's release (111.0), 29970 entries
could_see.rule: for each database that was run, the Family entries in which the tool's entry list has a signature of it ('with'), or those in which it has none ('without'), whichever is shorter, as accessions parted by spaces; an entry that the tool's list does not hold has no signature of any database

check_of_the_list.of: every signature of the outputs, with the InterPro entry the outputs give it, against the tool's own entry list

interpro.name: InterPro
interpro.text: InterPro: which member database's signature belongs to which InterPro entry, as the tool's own entry list and outputs give it, and the names and types of the entries at the dossier's release
interpro.licence: CC0 1.0 (InterPro's licence page: all of the InterPro, Pfam, PRINTS and SFLD downloadable data is freely available under CC0 1.0 Universal)
interpro.citation: Blum and others (2025) InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2025. Nucleic Acids Res 53:D444-D456.
interpro.citation_from: the atlas's own list of sources (data/proteins/atlases/planarian.json), from Europe PMC's record of the paper

pfam.name: Pfam
pfam.text: Pfam: its signatures (profile hidden Markov models) and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins
pfam.licence: CC0 1.0 (InterPro's licence page; Pfam's own page: freely available under the Creative Commons Zero licence)
pfam.citation: Paysan-Lafosse and others (2024) The Pfam protein families database: embracing AI/ML. Nucleic Acids Research. doi:10.1093/nar/gkae997. PMID 39540428.
pfam.citation_from: Pfam's own page on citing it, the first of its latest publications (saved as cite_pfam_citing.html)

prints.name: PRINTS
prints.text: PRINTS: its fingerprints and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins
prints.citation: Attwood and others (2012) The PRINTS database: a fine-grained protein sequence annotation and analysis resource - its status in 2012. Database (Oxford) 2012:bas019. doi:10.1093/database/bas019. PMID 22508994.
prints.citation_from: InterPro's page on PRINTS (saved as cite_interpro_prints.html)

sfld.name: SFLD
sfld.text: SFLD (the Structure-Function Linkage Database): its signatures and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins
sfld.citation_asked: InterPro's page on SFLD names no publication (saved as cite_interpro_sfld.html)

hamap.name: HAMAP
hamap.text: HAMAP (SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics): its family profiles and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins
hamap.licence: CC BY 4.0 (HAMAP's own page: distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY 4.0) License)
hamap.citation: HAMAP in 2015: updates to the protein family classification and annotation system. Nucleic Acids Res. 43:D1064-D1070 (2015).
hamap.citation_from: HAMAP's own page, which asks for it in these words

gene3d.name: CATH-Gene3D
gene3d.text: CATH-Gene3D: its domain models and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins
gene3d.licence: CC BY 4.0 (CATH's own pages: the CATH Protein Structure Classification Database is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)
gene3d.citation_asked: CATH's licence page names the database's authors and no paper, and its publications page gave no text that could be read (saved as cite_cath_publications.html)

ncbifam.name: NCBIfam
ncbifam.text: NCBIfam (NCBI, with TIGRFAMs): its protein family models and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins; named as NCBIfam's wherever they are used
ncbifam.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike), as NCBI's page on TIGRFAMs states: TIGRFAMs data are made available under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license
ncbifam.citation: Li W, O'Neill KR, Haft DH and others (2021) RefSeq: expanding the Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline reach with protein family model curation. Nucleic Acids Res 49(D1):D1020-D1028. PMID 33270901.
ncbifam.citation_from: NCBI's page on TIGRFAMs, which asks for the most recent publication describing NCBI's Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline and lists this one first among its references

panther.name: PANTHER
panther.text: PANTHER: its family models and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins; named as PANTHER's wherever they are used
panther.licence: CC BY 4.0 for its data and data products, as PANTHER's terms page states; the page was read in a browser on 18 November 2026, its site refusing automated reads; its models as distributed with InterProScan may be copied and redistributed freely in accordance with InterPro's copyright agreement
panther.citation_asked: PANTHER's site refuses automated reads, and its terms page, read in a browser, names no paper

cdd.name: CDD
cdd.text: CDD (NCBI's Conserved Domain Database): its domain models and the tool's matches of them on the planarian's proteins; named as CDD's wherever they are used
cdd.licence: No open licence stated: CDD's own page states no terms, and NCBI's policies page none for CDD itself; it was decided on 18 November 2026 that a database whose provider states no terms may be used for this scan where it is publicly available
cdd.citation_asked: NCBI's help page for CDD lists a section on citing it, whose text is not in the saved page (cite_cdd_help.html)

antifam.name: AntiFam
antifam.text: AntiFam: its models of spurious protein predictions, counted only (it has no InterPro entries)
antifam.licence: CC0 1.0 (InterPro's page on AntiFam: freely available under the Creative commons Zero (CC0) licence)
antifam.citation: Ruth Y Eberhardt, Dan Haft, Marco Punta, Maria Martin, Claire O'Donovan, Alex Bateman. (2012) AntiFam: A tool to help identify spurious ORFs in protein annotation. Database:bas003. PMID: 22434837.
antifam.citation_from: InterPro's page on AntiFam, which asks for it in these words
